Tom —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our call, I attached three commitment structures that map to the usage profile you shared (heavy nightly batch scoring + steady daytime inference). High-level options below; the spreadsheet has per-token economics and burn projections.

Option 1 — Soft-floor starter (conservative)
- Cluster: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum anchor: 8 GPUs (soft floor)
- Ramp cadence: immediate 50% activation month 1, full by month 3
- Warm-start credits: 200k token credits for first 60 days
- Notes: lowest monthly commitment, higher per-token rate after floor

Option 2 — Midline staircase (recommended)
- Cluster: 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum anchor: 12 GPUs (hard floor during business hours)
- Ramp cadence: 30% month 1, 65% month 2, 100% month 4
- Burst pool: access to +8 GPUs for short bursts (subject to availability)
- Warm-start credits: 500k token credits + one onboarding burst window
- Notes: balances unit cost and headroom for growth; recommended for production SLA

Option 3 — Growth lane (aggressive)
- Cluster: 32 x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum anchor: 20 GPUs (soft/hybrid floor)
- Ramp cadence: 25% month 1, 50% month 2, 75% month 3, 100% month 6
- Dedicated burst buffer and priority routing
- Warm-start credits: 1.2M token credits + 2 onboarding burst windows
- Notes: best unit economics for heavy throughput; higher commitment required

A few clarifying points:
- We can structure the commitment as a staircase with predetermined activation triggers (usage-based or fixed-date).
- Fallback policy: if dedicated capacity is constrained we’ll route to compatible hosted variants with automatic cache warmup to preserve latency SLOs.
- SLA: 99.9% availability for Dedicated pools; longer uptime windows available for the growth lane (see SLA_Terms_Redline.pdf).

Next steps: please indicate which option you prefer and whether you want a usage-triggered activation or fixed-date activation. If helpful, we can do a 30-minute sync tomorrow to lock rollout dates.
